$what: Provenance of aeon-effects-channel-bands.json — aeon's GENERATED declaration of the screen band each raster patch channel is confined to (`patchable(lo:, hi:)`), vendored into Aurora at a named aeon revision. src/core/formats/effects/channel-bands.ts imports it; src/renderer/providers/effects-preset.ts turns it into the ONE sentence an author sees when a sweep's peak-to-peak travel cannot fit its channel's band.
$why_vendored_into_src_and_not_test_fixt: It is not a test fixture. This file is READ AT RUNTIME by the editor — the warning under the `Travel` select is computed from it — so it must sit where the renderer bundle can import it, beside the other two contract documents this repo vendors (aurora-effects-preset.schema.json, aurora-effects-scene.schema.json) and for the same reason. Its drift gate is therefore the SCHEMA's shape (test/formats/effects-channel-bands-drift.test.ts, modelled on effects-preset-schema-drift.test.ts) and not test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts, whose table is scoped to test/fixtures.
$why_a_sidecar_at_all: Bar 19. A test that reads a peer's WORKING TREE has its colour decided by that peer's uncommitted edits — see docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md. The bytes are copied here at a COMMITTED revision, the peer's own git blob id is recorded so the pin is CHECKABLE rather than merely copied, and the separate question 'is that pin still what aeon ships' gets its own check that reads aeon at a committed revision, names it, fails on drift, and skips loudly when it cannot run.

what_this_document_is_authoritative_FOR_.authoritative_for: The per-channel band (`lo`, `hi`, `lines`) and the ASYMMETRIC edge behaviour, which no other artifact in the suite states in machine-readable form.
what_this_document_is_authoritative_FOR_.one_directional_only: `how_to_use` is explicit and the code obeys it: travel > lines is a CERTAIN refusal; travel <= lines is CANNOT TELL and NEVER a clearance, because the latched line is (anchor - Camera_Y) and where the sweep sits inside [lo, hi] is camera-dependent and unknowable at author time. `AnchorBandFit` in channel-bands.ts has no `fits` member AT THE TYPE LEVEL so a future edit cannot paint one by accident.
what_this_document_is_authoritative_FOR_.units_are_not_converted: `units` says SCREEN LINES, 1:1 with the authored patchable(lo:, hi:), and 'Do not convert' — the engine's single -1 is already applied in Raster_BuildSchedule. Nothing on Aurora's path adds or removes a 1; the module asserts that sentence is still in the file at load.
what_this_document_is_authoritative_FOR_.game_scoped: `game` is `sonic4`. The document declares bands for THAT game's raster module; channels 2 and 3 exist (RASTER_MAX_PATCH is 4) and are simply not declared, which is CANNOT TELL and never a warning.
